subject: Usage Question (Advice on Reshape) & Possible Memory Problems

messages.author: 5ba36a7ec005add4
messages.subject: Usage Question (Advice on Reshape) & Possible Memory Problems
parts:
Hello all,

I am having two (perhaps related) problems using the "reshape"
library. First, I do not know if I am calling it in the best way to
make it do what I want. I'll give the shape of my data, example code,
and my objectives to ask this question. Second, I am running out of
RAM. This may be related to possible mis-use of the library, but as I
am inexperienced with R I can't really tell. I will give object.size
numbers and the size of my dataset to ask this question.

Question 1:

My dataset is spectra of mineral samples from three different
wavelength ranges. For R purposes, this means that I have three
dataframes, each dataframe has nrow = to 596 (the number of spots per
sample (5) by the number of samples) and ncol = 2048 (pixel
intensities in the spectra). This data is much longer than I am used
to working with, usually I work with very tall data (N >> p). Since I
would like to make predictions of sample element composition (held in
another, less problematic data frame) from all chunks of the spectra,
I need a way to combine these three data frames into one, with the
rows being spot number and sample ID, and the columns from all the
different spectra appended together.

I was hoping to use reshape for this, because I also need to do some
normalization, aggregation, etc, along with this operation, and I
think that reshape produces very elegant code in that use case.

Anyway, once I read in the dataset, I use melt with no arguments on
each frame. This actually gives me the ID variables I want (sample ID
and spot being analyzed)

melted.data.uv <- melt(cset.list[[1]])
melted.data.vis <- melt(cset.list[[2]])
melted.data.vnir <- melt(cset.list[[3]])

Rowbind all the melted data together:

tmp <- rbind(melted.data.uv, melted.data.vis)
melted.data.all <- rbdind(tmp,melted.data.vnir)

And attempt to cast:

test.case <- cast(melted.data.all, name + spot ~ ...)

This works *perfectly* with one sample, I get exactly the shape that I
want out at the end, with very little code, and I'm excited about
integrating data pre-processing into the reshape functions. This part
of my question is really more of a "sanity check" than anything else:
is the reshape library appropriate for this use-case? Is there
something else that I am missing? Are there built-in functions that
would do this about as easily? This leads into:

Question #2:

The "cast" on my last line of code runs out of RAM, on my 16GB of RAM
computer. Here is the output of an object.size on the list of three
dataframes that my data-reading routines make:

> object.size(cset.list)
29984256 bytes

(about 29Mb) Given my nrow per dataframe (596) and ncol per dataframe,
(2048), is the behavior of reshape here "unexpected?" I don't
understand why it would run out of ram on such a small dataset, which
is why I'm suspicious of my usage of the library.

In any case, thanks very much for your time. If additional information
would help diagnose what's going on here, I'd be happy to provide it.

Cheers,

Mog

second question, reshape was one of my earliest R programming efforts
and so is not very efficient. I've had some ideas more recently on
how to make it much more efficient but unfortunately I've not had a
chance to implement them yet.
